clue.text: Bread from dining room sent back after tea

parts.note: cha is an informal word for tea

indicators.note: sent back tells us to read the room's word in the opposite direction

parts.note: a hall is a large room for communal dining, as in a college

explanation.surface: Someone at table has the bread returned from the dining room once tea is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses the room word; 'after' places it behind the tea word. CHA is a crossword favourite for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Challah is a braided Jewish loaf eaten on the Sabbath, a kind of bread.

clue.text: Old man cutting wire with skill

indicators.note: the father cuts into the wire, sitting inside it

parts.note: a cable is a wire
pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

explanation.surface: Dad cuts through a cable with expertise.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable means competent, having the ability or skill to do something.

clue.text: Intense musicale disrupted contemplative period

indicators.note: the concert's letters are broken up and rearranged, as an event is disrupted

explanation.surface: A powerful musical evening is interrupted by a time for reflection.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute's silence is held to remember the dead, a short span of reflection.

clue.text: Relaxed game ends on schedule

parts.note: loo is an old card game

indicators.note: the ends of schedule are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A laid-back match finishes on time.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is an old card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose and relaxed both describe something slack, not tight or strict.

clue.text: Bloke caught out, venture being random

indicators.note: out says the caught letter is taken away from the bloke

parts.note: chap means bloke
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
to hazard is to venture, as in hazarding a guess

explanation.surface: A man dismissed in cricket takes a chance on a wild shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught out' suggests cricket but strips C from CHAP, leaving HAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Haphazard means lacking plan or order, so done at random.

clue.text: Excellent sects from the east in island nation

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading right to left, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, with the figure 1 written as the letter I
cults are sects

explanation.surface: Fine religious groups arriving from the east settle in a small island country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' reverses A1 (with 1 as I) plus CULTS, giving STLUCIA.
explanation.definitionFit: St Lucia is an independent Caribbean island state, so a nation that is an island.

clue.text: Yankee stops lecturers travelling up for meeting

indicators.note: the letter stops up the lecturers, plugging a gap inside them
in a down clue, travelling up means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: dons are university lecturers
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American blocks academics heading north to a conference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling up' turns DONS into SNOD, and 'stops' puts Y inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of church officials, a formal meeting.

clue.text: We initial changes to prepare ambush

indicators.note: the two words change their order of letters to form the answer

explanation.surface: Our first moves are rearranged so we can set a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in wait is to hide ready to attack, which is setting an ambush.

clue.text: Doctor at this place? Go to small medical institution

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the words' letters are altered into the answer

explanation.surface: A doctor works here; go to this little clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun in a medical scene but is a verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage hospital is a small rural hospital, a modest medical establishment.

clue.text: American Satan devouring Republican alongside

indicators.note: the devil swallows the Republican, who ends up inside

parts.note: the Beast is a name for Satan, from Revelation

explanation.surface: A US devil swallows a party politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Abreast means side by side, level with someone, so alongside them.

clue.text: Rotten people sin to produce malicious missive

indicators.note: the three words are worked into something new, so their letters are rearranged to produce the answer

explanation.surface: Nasty folk sinning end up writing a spiteful letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotten' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'to produce' is the indicator acting on all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A poison-pen letter is an anonymous spiteful letter, a malicious piece of mail.

clue.text: Black couple to protect composer reversing in road

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: reversing tells us the couple-plus-composer group is read backwards
the pair surrounds the composer as if protecting him

parts.note: a duo is a couple
Maurice Ravel was a French composer

explanation.surface: A dark-clad pair shields a musician who is backing his car in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to protect' wraps the couple round the composer, then 'reversing' turns that whole group backwards to follow the black letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A boulevard is a broad city avenue, a type of road.

clue.text: One bounding area that separates two major cities

indicators.note: the area letter sits between the two cities, keeping them apart

parts.note: NY is New York and LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Something leaping across the land that divides two great American cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One bounding' suggests a leaper or a border, but it is a leaping antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is an African antelope, an animal that moves in leaps and bounds.

clue.text: Russian female revolutionary in American election

indicators.note: revolutionary says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the name lies inside the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Russian woman with radical views turns up in a US vote.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' unused; it is the hiding signal, and 'revolutionary' turns the hidden run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Elena is a common Russian girl's name, the local form of Helen.

clue.text: Diversion giving an essential cover for English soldiers?

indicators.note: the essential wraps round the English soldiers like a cover

parts.note: a must is an essential
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A vital protection for British troops turns out to be just entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'cover for' is a containment signal rather than military protection.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusement is entertainment, something that diverts or passes the time pleasantly.

clue.text: Quietly detests being involved in key software trial

indicators.note: the quiet loathing ends up inside the key, involved in it

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
hates means detests

explanation.surface: Someone silently loathes getting caught up in a crucial program test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' is not a vital point but the Alt key; P plus HATES goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpha test is the first, in-house round of testing a program, a software trial.

clue.text: Revolting animals were so stubborn!

definitions.meaning: in Orwell's Animal Farm the animals who revolt are led by pigs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' means rebelling, not disgusting: in Animal Farm the pigs headed the uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig-headed describes obstinate refusal to change one's mind, the same as stubborn.

clue.text: Neglected animal given signal amid tangled gorse

indicators.note: amid places the signalled word inside the jumbled shrub
tangled means the shrub's letters are knotted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
cued means given a signal, as an actor is

explanation.surface: A neglected creature found tangled in a gorse bush is given a sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangled' scrambles the shrub into RESOG, and 'amid' sets the signalled word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescue dog is one taken in after neglect or abandonment, so a neglected animal saved.

clue.text: Mechanical device skinned fantasy author

indicators.note: skinning removes the outside, so the author's outer letters go

parts.note: Terry Pratchett wrote the Discworld fantasy novels

explanation.surface: A gadget flays a writer of fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinned' removes the first and last letters of PRATCHETT.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratchet is a toothed mechanism that lets motion go one way only, a mechanical device.

clue.text: God needing name for Germanic character

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A deity needs a name before he can become a figure of Germanic myth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' is a written letter, not a person: thorn is the rune for the 'th' sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorn is a letter of the old runic and Old English alphabets, a Germanic character.

clue.text: Folded card husband lost in TV fundraiser turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom, so backwards
lost says the husband letter goes missing from the fundraiser

parts.note: a telethon is a long television broadcast raising money for charity

explanation.surface: A greetings card goes astray when a husband disappears during a charity broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes H from TELETHON to give TELETON, and 'turned up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded card with a printed picture, used for short letters.

clue.text: Net profit at last drawn that voids margins

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of profit
voiding the margins strips the outer letters from the word for drawn

parts.note: pulled means drawn, as a cart is drawn

explanation.surface: Net profit ends up being drawn down once the margins are emptied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Net' looks like accounting but is the definition. 'that voids margins' removes the P and D of PULLED, leaving ULLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulle is a fine netting fabric used for veils, so it is a net.

clue.text: Approaches snooker table but loses form?

definitions.meaning: humorously, a player who ... walks up to the table to pot a ball
to go to pot is to deteriorate or go to ruin

explanation.surface: A snooker player walks up to the table but his game is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is whimsical: in snooker, to pot is to sink a ball, so heading for the table is 'going to pot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to pot is an idiom for declining badly, as a player who has lost form does.

clue.text: Peer outside entrance to Lords in coat

indicators.note: the gazing word goes outside, wrapping the letter from Lords

parts.note: to peer is to gaze

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A nobleman in his robe waits outside the door of the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' is a verb here, not a member of the Lords; 'outside' wraps GAZE round L.
explanation.definitionFit: A glaze is a glossy layer applied over pottery or pastry, a coat.

clue.text: Finnish port one from Ankara found acceptable

parts.note: Ankara is the capital of Turkey, so someone from there is a Turk
U means upper-class and so socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A Turkish visitor is found welcome in a Finnish harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: U for 'acceptable' comes from the old British U and non-U distinction in upper-class speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Turku is a city and harbour on the southwest coast of Finland.

clue.text: Two kids lost? New angle: three lads lost!

indicators.note: the second lost says the letters have strayed into a jumble and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two children have gone missing, and somebody suggests a fresh line: three boys have vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'lost' belongs to the definition; the second is the anagram signal on N plus ANGLE THREE LADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hansel and Gretel are the fairy-tale brother and sister abandoned in the forest, two children astray.

clue.text: Time pressure on in war zone

parts.note: heat means pressure, as in 'the heat is on'
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: Time pressure bears down on soldiers in a combat area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressure on' looks like one phrase but splits into two pieces; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre of war is the region where fighting happens, so a theatre is a war zone.

clue.text: Characters seen in flannelette or cotton garment?

definitions.text: Characters seen in flannelette or cotton
definitions.meaning: a ..., two Ts together, appears in both fabric names
a close-fitting jacket once worn by men

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as DOUBLE T: both fabric words contain TT. The fabric surface points to clothing, which is the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet is a man's fitted jacket of the Renaissance period, an item of clothing.
